parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans expression, no documented border/document friction, no trans-specific violence record, and no universal facility exclusion. Courts demonstrably work for trans people (sterilisation condition struck down 2024; supreme court vulnerability-assessment safeguard for detained trans foreigners; document reissues), and the 2009 anti-discrimination law covers gender identity in services. Against that: head-of-state and ministerial threat-framing of trans people, organised public hostility, LGBTQ-wide discrimination prevalence (not trans-specific, 2023), and — most serious — prison/detention placement documented as unprepared and unresolved, with lower-court practice inconsistent beneath the supreme-court safeguard. That detention exposure is traveler-relevant but low-probability; the official hostility raises the severity of social outing. Rural/late-night harassment noted. Net: protections exist and partially operate, but a documented unresolved state placement gap plus high-level hostility holds this at the lower end of Reduced Risk.
